title: Soup Sieve untrusted selector compilation can exhaust CPU
summary: Crafted CSS digit escapes trigger exponential regex backtracking during selector compilation, including through Beautiful Soup. This differs from the descendant-matching issue already recorded separately.

severity.rationale: Exposure requires untrusted selector strings, rather than untrusted markup alone. The documented impact is denial of service in the worker, warranting a 30-day response.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.

affected.note: Vendor advisory lists <=2.9.2; the reviewed database lists <=2.10. Both identify the fix in 3.0, but the database recommends 3.0.2 or later because 3.0 was yanked.

exposure: Scraping and extraction tools that compile attacker-controlled selectors are exposed. Developer-controlled selectors do not meet this prerequisite.

params.instructions: Check the installed soupsieve version and whether untrusted selectors reach compile() or BeautifulSoup.select(). Treat 2.x as affected; use 3.0.2 or later for upgrading.

remediation.details: Use 3.0.2 or later on Python 3.11.5 or later. The changelog requires that Python minimum because older interpreters have broken possessive quantifiers.
remediation.risk: Medium. The 3.0 series changes selector behavior and drops Python 3.10 support.

verification: Confirm the loaded package and Python versions; test normal extraction rules after upgrading.
